evals.name: device-entry-drives-the-app
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment ios. orchestrate.config.yaml's environments.entries.ios has platform ios, app com.example.app, and the steps stackUp (builds, installs and runs the app on the simulator), stackDown (uninstalls it), seed and auth. The plan lists R1, a settings toggle that persists after the app is reopened. agent-device and ffmpeg are installed.
evals.expected_output: Exports AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION before stackUp, runs stackUp, seed and auth, opens the app with agent-device open com.example.app --platform ios --relaunch, drives the toggle through agent-device with snapshot -i and press --settle, cites get or is output as evidence, names the device and its OS version on the scenario's recording, runs no phone replay, closes with agent-device close, and ends with the return contract's JSON block.
expectations: Exports AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION before running stackUp
Opens the app with agent-device open com.example.app --platform ios --relaunch after seed and auth, built from the entry's app and platform fields
Every check's result rests on the output of an agent-device get, is or wait command, and each check cites the promoted frame that shows it, or a reading of that output where no frame shows it
The scenario's recording names the device and its OS version, and the return names the app id and platform
Step 8 runs agent-device close
No scenario carries a phone replay recording
anti_expectations: Runs agent-browser
Asserts through eval

evals.name: missing-agent-device-blocks-with-the-token
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment android, whose entry has platform android and app com.example.app. agent-device is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Returns status BLOCKED with report null and a reason opening no-agent-device: that names the install hint npm i -g agent-device@latest, and lists every scenario it could not prove in gaps[] against its requirement.
expectations: The JSON block's status is exactly BLOCKED
The reason opens with no-agent-device:
The reason contains npm i -g agent-device@latest
report is null and every unproven requirement has a gaps[] entry
anti_expectations: Writes BLOCKED:no-agent-device as the status
Prints the agent-browser install hint
Writes a proof report

evals.name: device-attacks-and-visual-answers
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment ios, an entry with platform ios and app com.example.app, verifying a form screen the plan builds to a frame drawn at phone width. The app and drivers are installed and Step 2 has filmed the form scenario.
evals.expected_output: Step 5 drives background-and-return (agent-device home, then agent-device open com.example.app --platform ios without --relaunch) and rotate (agent-device orientation landscape-left, then portrait) on the form screen; the scenario's visualMatch records contrast and sideways scroll as not measurable on this surface and measures every driven control's short side from get attrs against 44px.
expectations: Runs agent-device home followed by agent-device open com.example.app --platform ios without --relaunch, and asserts the form state survived
Runs agent-device orientation landscape-left, shoots the screen, then restores portrait
visualMatch answers contrast and sideways scroll as not measurable on this surface
Every control the walk drove has a get attrs rect cited against the 44px rule
anti_expectations: Marks contrast or sideways scroll as clean on a device scenario
Uses set viewport or set device on a device scenario
Skips the rotate or the background-and-return attack

evals.name: stack-that-will-not-start-blocks-with-no-infra
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment local, whose stackUp command exits non-zero twice with a port-in-use error and whose stackStatus keeps reporting the stack down.
evals.expected_output: Returns status BLOCKED with report null, a reason opening no-infra: that names the service and quotes the command as it ran, and no proof report, prose report-back or scenario walk.
expectations: The JSON block's status is exactly BLOCKED and report is null
The reason opens with no-infra: and names the service and the command that failed
Retries stackUp once and stops after the second failure
anti_expectations: Writes BLOCKED:no-infra as the status
Drives any scenario or writes a proof report
Assumes a port and continues

evals.name: verdict-is-derived-from-coverage
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x on the last round. The docs list R1, R2 and R3. Your walks proved R1 and R2 with SUCCESS scenarios and R3 could not be reached because its feature flag is off in this environment, and every walk you drove felt like a pass.
evals.expected_output: coverage[] holds one row per requirement, R3 is NOT VERIFIED with a gaps[] entry naming the flag, and verdict is PARTIAL with the status PARTIAL and the summary sentence that QA could not verify 1 of 3 requirements.
expectations: coverage[] has exactly one row for each of R1, R2 and R3
verdict is PARTIAL because a requirement is NOT VERIFIED and no scenario is a FAILURE
gaps[] has one entry for R3 whose mechanism names the feature flag and the line that reads it
anti_expectations: Writes verdict PASS because the driven walks passed
Drops R3 from coverage[]
Backfills R3 with an adjacent passing check

evals.name: fail-with-rounds-left-defers-the-report
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x with round 1 of rounds 3. One scenario reproduces a bug: the total is wrong after a discount is applied.
evals.expected_output: Writes the bug's scenario and ledger line, returns status FAIL with report null and one bugs[] entry carrying id, summary, trigger and hint, builds no videos, writes no proof report, and leaves the stack, fixtures and staging dir in place for the fix round.
expectations: status is FAIL and report is null
bugs[] has one entry whose id is the scenario number and whose askUser is false
No report-media run and no proof-report.html
The stack is left running and the return says so
anti_expectations: Writes proof-report.html on this round
Tears down the stack or deletes verify-staging
Returns FAIL with an empty bugs[]

evals.name: run-log-is-append-only
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x on round 2. verification/run-log.jsonl holds round 1 lines for scenarios 01 and 02; 02 was a FAILURE and the fix round closed its bug. Nothing else changed in git.
evals.expected_output: Re-drives 02 only, clears its old frames first, appends a new line for 02 with round 2, carries 01 unchanged from its ledger line into the report, and never edits or removes an existing line.
expectations: Deletes verification/screenshots/02_* before driving 02 again
Appends one new line for 02 carrying round 2 and the current commits
Scenario 01 is transcribed from its round 1 line without being driven
Every round 1 line is still present and unchanged
anti_expectations: Rewrites or truncates run-log.jsonl
Re-drives 01
Restamps 01's line with round 2

evals.name: browser-walk-replays-on-a-phone
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The change added a filter to a list page and the project says the app serves phones.
evals.expected_output: Drives the filter flow on desktop, then, once every desktop scenario is filmed, opens a second named session, sets it to agent-browser set device "iPhone 14" and signs in again there, and drives the same flow to its closing assert as one more recording of the same scenario, under that scenario's number with the recording's prefix. The replay's crop reads as a portrait picture in Step 6, and Step 8 closes both sessions by name.
expectations: The scenario carries phone.replay required with a one-line why, decided before the first walk
The flow is replayed after set device "iPhone 14", and the replay is a second entry in the same scenario's recordings[], its files named NN_SLUG-phone, with size phone
The replay runs after every desktop scenario, in a named session of its own that ran its own setup
The replay is driven from its first click to the same closing assert as desktop
The replay asserts documentElement.scrollWidth minus clientWidth is 0
Step 8 closes the desktop session and the phone session, each by name
anti_expectations: Narrows the viewport instead of setting a device
Shoots only the final screen on the phone
Skips the replay because desktop passed
Lists the phone replay as a scenario of its own
Sets the phone device in the desktop session and tries to restore it afterwards

evals.name: device-walk-replays-on-each-listed-device
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment ios, an entry with platform ios, app com.example.app, devices ["iPhone 17 Pro", "iPad Pro 13-inch (M4)"] and a stackUp of make ios-run DEVICE={DEVICE}. The plan lists R1, a list screen with a detail view. Both simulators exist and agent-device and ffmpeg are installed.
evals.expected_output: Runs stackUp twice, once per device name, opens the app on each device in its own session (feat-x-iphone-17-pro and feat-x-ipad-pro-13-inch-m4) with --device, drives the list-to-detail flow on the iPhone and again on the iPad as a second recording of the same scenario, keeps one coverage row for R1 naming that scenario, names each device and its OS version on its recording, and closes both sessions.
expectations: Runs make ios-run DEVICE=iPhone 17 Pro and make ios-run DEVICE=iPad Pro 13-inch (M4), with the placeholder filled
Exports a different AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION per device and opens the app with --device on each
The iPad replay is driven from its first press to the same closing assert and joins the scenario's recordings[], naming the iPad as its device
coverage[] has one row for R1 naming the one scenario
Each recording names its device and OS version
Runs agent-device close once per device session
anti_expectations: Drives the iPad by shooting only the final screen
Opens both devices in one session
Writes two coverage rows for R1
Lists the iPad replay as a scenario of its own

evals.name: browser-scenario-is-scouted-then-filmed-in-one-take
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x, the only round, against a web environment. The feature adds a filter to a list page: choosing a status narrows the rows to that status. Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Scouts the filter flow with the recorder off, returns the page to its opening state, then films the scenario as one take: agent-browser record start with --cursor writing NN_SLUG.mp4 beside the report, one batch with --bail that holds the opening state for about a second and a half, in which every click is click SELECTOR --human followed by a wait on a condition, an assert and a screenshot to staging, a closing hold of about a second and a half on the final state, then record stop as its own command. Promotes the take's frames after reading them, writes the scenario's steps as a summary of the take in order, each with the checks it brings about and each check's result from the take's asserts, adds the take to recordings[] with its video named on the scenario's ledger line, and in Step 6 the report-media script prints ok NN_SLUG.mp4 recorded for it, with the sizes where it compressed the recording.
expectations: The recorder starts only after the flow has been driven once without it
The take is one batch, and record stop runs as a separate command after it
Every click in the take is written as click with --human, and the recording is started with --cursor
Each step in the take waits on a condition before its assert and screenshot
The scenario's ledger line names NN_SLUG.mp4 as its recording's video before Step 6 runs
The scenario's title, its given and the text of every check are written from the docs before the flow is driven
The scenario's steps summarise the take's user actions in the order the take ran them, written after the take counted, and every step carries at least one check
Every check has a result of pass or fail from the take's asserts, and each check shown on screen cites the promoted frame that shows it
The title is the question the scenario answers, given is a list with one setup fact a line, and each step and each check is one plain sentence
The take holds on the opening state before its first action and on the final state after its last, about a second and a half each
A design drawn at another width for a state the take passed through is re-shot after the take, recorder off, by replaying the scouted steps to that state

Every sentence in the scenario reads to a Product or QA person who has never seen the code: told from the user's side, naming controls by their on-screen labels and records, users and values by their kind

Each proof is a promoted frame or a reading from a named source, gives the reader confidence its check alone does not, and is cited by exactly one check; a reading's raw holds only the values its check rests on, in at most fifteen lines, and its found says why it counts

The primary journeys have the group journey, every other scenario sits under a short broad heading naming the kind of check it is, free of this feature's own terms, and a behaviour an e2e test already asserts is filmed from that test with no browser walk of its own
Before any text is typed in the take, the pointer travels to the field and clicks it, and the text arrives a few words at a time
A target off screen is brought into view by a smooth scroll before the pointer travels to it
Where a step opens another tab, the take restarts the recorder there as the next numbered file, PREFIX.fileK.mp4, and Step 6 joins the files into one video
Every frame the recording lists was shot during the take, so it is also in the video
anti_expectations: Starts the recorder before the flow is known, so retries and dead ends are in the video
Uses snapshot refs as targets inside the take
Keeps the video of a take in which a step failed or an assert returned an unexpected value
Builds the browser scenario's video from its screenshots while its recorder works
Writes the scenario's steps before the take, or as a summary that does not follow the video
Marks a check passed on an interpretation instead of on what an assert returned
Writes given, the steps or the checks as paragraphs
Names the ids, names or amounts the run used in title, given, a step or a check
Says how the run was filmed or driven in title, given, a step or a check
Starts or ends the video mid-motion, with no time to read the first or the last state
Changes the take, or cuts the video, to get the design re-shoot
Puts field names, status codes, selectors, identifiers or an assert's raw return in title, given, a step, a check, claim or found
Uses fill, hover, scrollintoview or a bare mouse move for an action inside the take
Leaves the recording on the first tab and shoots the new tab only as a screenshot after the take

evals.name: wording-change-owes-no-phone-replay
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The change reworded the help text of one control on an existing page and the project says the app serves phones.
evals.expected_output: Plans the scenario, sets its phone.replay to not needed with a why saying the change leaves the page laid out as it was, films the desktop take, and opens no phone session.
expectations: The scenario carries phone.replay not needed and a one-line why, written before the first walk
The scenario has one recording, the desktop take
No phone session is opened or closed
anti_expectations: Replays the flow on a phone
Leaves the scenario without a phone decision

evals.name: third-party-screen-with-nobody-to-sign-in
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The change makes the product post a message carrying a link to an outside chat service, and the link opens a page of the product. The stack skill says this stack delivers to the real service. No sign-in is saved and the run's interaction policy is off.
evals.expected_output: Proves what the product sent from the request in a Step 3 scenario, gives the check on the chat service's screen a scenario naming that service as its thirdParty and grades it NOT VERIFIED with a reason and a gaps[] entry saying nobody could be asked, drives the linked page as a scenario of its own opened at the address the product sent, and returns PARTIAL.
expectations: A headless scenario proves the message and its link from the request the product sent
The scenario on the chat service's screen carries thirdParty, has no recording and no check result, and is NOT VERIFIED
Its gaps[] entry says nobody could be asked and names the sign-in as what would close it
The linked page is driven as its own scenario, opened at the address the product sent
The round carries on and returns PARTIAL
anti_expectations: Builds a page that imitates the chat service and films it
Marks a check on the chat service's screen as passed
Asks the user to sign in
Returns BLOCKED or stops the round

evals.name: flow-across-a-service-and-a-background-wait
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x, the only round, against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The change lets a user start a job from a page of the product. The job runs in the background for a few minutes, then posts its result to an outside chat service, where the user reads it. The stack delivers to the real service and a saved sign-in for it exists. Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Writes one scenario told in parts, one part per stretch that needs the one before, each with its own title, steps and video; stops the recorder through the background wait and resumes it on the result as a .wait file; Step 6 joins it behind a pause card; the last video ends on the result where the user reads it.
expectations: The scenario carries parts[], each with a title, its own steps and its own recordings[], and no top-level steps or recordings
The parts split where the flow moves to the chat service or picks up after the background work, and nowhere else
The take is stopped once the job's start is on screen and started again once the result has arrived, the later file named PREFIX.fileK.wait-SECONDS.mp4
The report-media run prints an ok line for that recording that says it joined its files with 1 wait
The video of the last part ends on the result shown on the chat service's own screen
The scenario's title is a question naming the user's action and the exact outcome they get
anti_expectations: Films the background wait end to end as still picture
Writes each stretch as a separate scenario with no link between them
Ends a video before the result arrives

evals.name: screen-check-proved-by-its-frame-alone
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x, the only round, against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The change makes the order page show a new total once the user edits a line of the order. The total is also stored in the database and returned by the product's API. Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Grades the total check from the take's assert and cites only the promoted frame that shows the new total; any reading in the scenario backs a check no frame shows.
expectations: The check on the new total cites one proof, the promoted frame that shows it
No proof of the API reply or the stored row backs a check that a frame already shows
Every proof with a raw backs a check no frame in the scenario shows
The scenario's title is a question naming the edit and the exact total the user should see
anti_expectations: A check cites both a frame and a reading of the same fact
The title is a statement or a topic with no expected outcome

evals.name: phone-replay-stays-inside-its-part
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x, the only round, against environment local, an entry with no platform field. The project says the app serves phones. The change adds a new confirmation screen the user reaches after leaving the product for an outside sign-in service and coming back. A saved sign-in for that service exists. Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Decides phone.replay required, tells the scenario in parts, and adds the phone replay as one more recording of the part whose screens it replays, labelled Phone with size phone, its checks under that part's steps.
expectations: The scenario carries phone.replay required with a one-line why
The phone replay is a recording in the recordings[] of the part whose screens it replays, labelled Phone, with size phone
No part holds only phone recordings
A check only the phone shows sits under the step of that part that reached its screen
anti_expectations: Adds a part titled for the phone
Writes the phone replay as a scenario of its own when its steps match the desktop take

evals.name: missing-access-asked-once-up-front
evals.prompt: You are running the qa stage of run feat-x as a subagent, the only round, against environment local, an entry with no platform field. Your brief says to send questions to the agent that started you. The feature posts a summary to an outside chat service the user reads there, and the stack calls a paid API whose key the project's env file leaves empty. No saved sign-in exists for the chat service. Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Lists every tool, key, account and sign-in the scenarios need before bringing anything up, finds the empty key and the missing sign-in, and sends one question to the agent that started it naming both and the scenarios that wait on each, asking for the key to be put in the env file rather than pasted.
expectations: Takes stock of access before the stack is brought up or any scenario is driven
Checks the key is set without printing its value
Sends one message to the agent that started it naming the empty key, the missing sign-in and the scenarios that wait on each
Asks for the key to be put in the env file, naming the variable, and asks whether the user will sign in when shown the browser
anti_expectations: Asks the user directly with its own question tool
Asks for the key's value in the chat
Asks a second time partway through a walk for something the access list should have named
Grades a scenario NOT VERIFIED for a missing key without having asked
